title: Coffee truffles
subtitle: dark chocolate ganache truffles with a sharp coffee note
excerpt: Coffee truffles are dark chocolate ganache made by stirring instant coffee into the hot cream before it goes onto the chocolate. The coffee sharpens against the dark chocolate without adding bitterness of its own. The ganache chills overnight, then is scooped into balls and rolled in cocoa powder.
sourceNotes: Coffee-flavoured dark chocolate truffles documented in British and continental confectionery from the mid-twentieth century onward. The instant coffee method is the standard home-kitchen approach; whole coffee beans steeped in cream and strained out give a cleaner flavour in professional recipes.

glossaryTerms.definition: A smooth emulsion of chocolate and hot cream. The ratio of chocolate to cream determines whether the ganache is used as a glaze (thin), a soft filling (medium), or a firm truffle (thick).

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze uncoated in a single layer, then transfer to a freezer bag for up to 2 months. Defrost overnight in the fridge and roll in cocoa before serving.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Keep in the fridge in an airtight container for up to 2 weeks. Bring to room temperature for 20 minutes before serving.

content.text: Coffee truffles are built around a dark chocolate

with instant coffee dissolved in the cream before it goes onto the chocolate. The coffee sharpens the flavour of the dark chocolate without adding bitterness of its own. The ganache must chill overnight until it is firm enough to scoop and roll.

Put the chopped chocolate and butter into a heatproof bowl. Heat the cream in a small saucepan over a medium heat until it just comes to the boil. Remove from the heat and stir in the instant coffee until dissolved.
Pour the hot coffee cream over the chocolate. Leave for 2 minutes, then stir slowly from the centre outward until smooth and glossy. Do not stir vigorously.
Press a sheet of cling film directly onto the surface of the ganache. Chill in the fridge for at least 8 hours or overnight, until the ganache is firm enough to scoop into balls.

Sieve the cocoa powder onto a flat plate. Scoop small amounts of ganache (about a heaped teaspoon each) and roll briefly between your palms into rough balls. Work quickly; the heat from your hands softens the ganache fast.
Drop each ball into the cocoa and roll to coat all over. Place on a lined tray. Refrigerate for 20 minutes to firm before serving or packing.

attrs.problem: Ganache oily and separated rather than smooth
attrs.avoid: Avoid stirring the ganache before leaving it to sit for 2 minutes; stirring too early cools one part of the mix faster than the other and splits the emulsion.
attrs.fix: Add a tablespoon of warm cream and stir very slowly from the centre outward. If it comes back together, continue slowly until smooth.

attrs.problem: Truffles melting and losing shape while rolling
attrs.avoid: Avoid rolling at room temperature if the kitchen is warm; soft ganache melts on contact with hands.
attrs.fix: Chill the ganache for longer before rolling, and chill your hands under cold water before starting. Work in small batches of 6 to 8 at a time.
